properties.natural_language: Before executing any contract code triggered by an external transaction, the EVM MUST enforce gas limits from the transaction to prevent unbounded resource consumption.

External transaction calldata MUST be treated as untrusted input; the EVM must handle all bytecode paths including encountering the INVALID opcode (0xfe) without crashing or entering an undefined state.
The gas limit provided with the external transaction MUST be validated as a non-negative integer within protocol bounds before contract execution begins.
When the INVALID opcode (0xfe) is executed, ALL remaining gas in the current execution context MUST be consumed, consistent with other EVM exception-throwing behavior.

When INVALID (0xfe) is encountered in a nested call context (CALL, DELEGATECALL), only the current call frame MUST revert; the parent execution context MUST receive a failure return value without being terminated.
Opcode 0xfe MUST remain permanently reserved for the INVALID instruction and MUST NOT be reassigned to any other functionality in any EVM version.
Compilers and development tooling MUST correctly emit opcode 0xfe only for intentional abort paths; accidental emission of INVALID MUST NOT occur in correctly compiled contracts.
Contract bytecode MUST be immutable after deployment; no mechanism SHALL allow injection of 0xfe (INVALID) into deployed contract bytecode.
After the INVALID opcode is executed, the EVM MUST be in a halted state with all state changes from the current execution context reverted.
After ACTION-REVERT-STATE executes, all state modifications from the current execution context MUST be rolled back and the transaction MUST be in a failed state.
After ACTION-CONSUME-ALL-GAS executes, the remaining gas counter MUST equal zero and no gas refund SHALL be issued.
After ACTION-CHARGE-GAS-3 executes successfully, the remaining gas MUST be reduced by exactly 3 units.
After ACTION-CHARGE-GAS-3 with insufficient gas, the execution MUST enter STATE-OUT-OF-GAS and halt with an exceptional failure.
After ACTION-READ-IMMEDIATE, the immediate operand byte MUST be the single byte at position pc+1 in the bytecode.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-RANGE detects an operand in the disallowed range, execution MUST enter STATE-RANGE-INVALID and halt with exceptional failure.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-STACK-DEPTH detects insufficient stack depth, execution MUST enter STATE-STACK-UNDERFLOW and halt.
After ACTION-EXECUTE-DUPN completes, stack[0] MUST contain a copy of the value previously at stack[n], and the stack depth MUST increase by 1.
After ACTION-EXECUTE-SWAPN completes, the values at stack[0] and stack[n+1] MUST be exchanged, with stack depth unchanged.
After ACTION-EXECUTE-EXCHANGE completes, the values at stack[n+1] and stack[m+1] MUST be exchanged, with stack depth unchanged.
After ACTION-INCREMENT-PC, the program counter MUST equal the previous PC value plus 2 (opcode + immediate byte).
After ACTION-CONSUME-ALL-GAS in error handling, remaining gas MUST be zero and the call frame state changes MUST be reverted.
After ACTION-PROPAGATE-FAILURE, the calling context MUST receive a failure status indicating the child frame halted exceptionally.
When the immediate operand position is beyond the code boundary, the operand MUST be treated as 0, consistent with PUSH opcode behavior.
An exceptional failure from DUPN, SWAPN, or EXCHANGE MUST consume all remaining gas and revert all state changes in the current call frame.
EVM stack implementations MUST support efficient O(1) indexed access to positions up to index 235 without performance degradation.
Static analysis tools MUST be able to track stack state accurately through DUPN, SWAPN, and EXCHANGE operations for security verification purposes.
Compilers generating DUPN, SWAPN, and EXCHANGE instructions MUST correctly compute stack indices; compiler bugs MUST NOT result in silent stack corruption.
For DUPN and SWAPN, operand byte values in the range (90, 128) exclusive MUST always be rejected to prevent conflicts with JUMPDEST and PUSH opcodes.
For EXCHANGE, operand byte values in the range (79, 128) exclusive MUST always be rejected.
The decode_single function MUST produce stack indices in the range 17-235 for all valid operand values.
Before processing any transaction from an external submitter, the transaction nonce MUST be extracted and validated against the 2^64-1 maximum.
Transaction data from external submitters MUST be treated as untrusted; nonce values MUST be validated as unsigned integers below 2^64-1 before any execution occurs.
After ACTION-CHECK-NONCE-LIMIT with nonce >= 2^64-1, the transaction MUST be rejected and MUST NOT produce any state changes.
After ACTION-INCREMENT-NONCE, the account nonce MUST equal exactly old_nonce + 1.
After ACTION-CHECK-SENDER-NONCE detects nonce at 2^64-1 for CREATE/CREATE2, the opcode MUST return 0 on the stack WITHOUT executing initcode and WITHOUT deducting initcode gas.
No account nonce SHALL ever exceed 2^64-1. This limit applies retroactively from genesis.
The nonce limit of 2^64-1 MUST be enforced retroactively from genesis block, regardless of EIP activation block.
When CREATE/CREATE2 fails due to nonce limit, only initcode execution gas MUST be skipped; other gas costs (base cost, memory expansion) MAY still be deducted.
No existing account on any Ethereum network SHALL have a nonce approaching 2^64-1 at the time of EIP activation.
Under normal transaction throughput limits, reaching nonce 2^64-1 MUST be practically impossible for any single account.
Applications using CREATE/CREATE2 MUST check the return value to detect silent creation failure due to nonce limits.
After ACTION-INCREMENT-NONCE during account creation, the new account MUST have nonce exactly equal to 1 before init code execution begins.
After ACTION-CHECK-EMPTY-ACCOUNTS, every touched account that has no code AND zero nonce AND zero balance MUST be identified for deletion.
After ACTION-DELETE-EMPTY-ACCOUNTS, all identified empty accounts MUST be converted to non-existent state.
After ACTION-CHECK-VALUE-TRANSFER determines value > 0 to a dead destination, 25,000 gas MUST be charged for account creation.
After ACTION-CHECK-VALUE-TRANSFER determines value == 0 to a dead destination, NO extra gas charge MUST be applied.
After ACTION-REVERT-DELETIONS on transaction revert, all accounts that were deleted during this transaction MUST be restored to their pre-transaction state.
No account SHALL transition from non-existent to existent-but-empty state. An account may only be created if it will have non-zero code, nonce, or balance.
Both successful and failed calls that access an account MUST count as 'touches' for the purposes of end-of-transaction empty account cleanup.
The protocol MUST prevent creation of empty accounts by simply not creating the account if it would result in an empty state (no code, zero nonce, zero balance).
If a CREATE operation reverts, the nonce increment from EIP-161 MUST also be reverted along with all other state changes.
All Ethereum client implementations MUST track touched accounts consistently during transaction execution to produce identical state roots.
State trie implementations MUST support efficient account deletion operations to avoid DoS vectors at transaction end.
Miner rewards and SELFDESTRUCT operations MUST be correctly identified as account touches for empty account cleanup purposes.
After ACTION-POP-STACK-VALUE, the stack depth MUST decrease by 1 and the popped value MUST be a 256-bit unsigned integer.
After ACTION-COUNT-LEADING-ZEROS, the result MUST be in the range [0, 256] where 256 is returned for input value 0.
After ACTION-PUSH-RESULT, the CLZ result MUST be on top of the stack and the stack depth MUST be unchanged from before the CLZ operation (1 popped, 1 pushed).
After ACTION-CHECK-GAS determines gas < 5, the EVM MUST enter out-of-gas state and halt execution.
After ACTION-DEDUCT-GAS, the remaining gas counter MUST be reduced by exactly 5 units.
After ACTION-RETURN-256 for zero input, the value 256 MUST be pushed onto the stack.
After ACTION-COMPUTE-CLZ-STANDARD for non-zero input, the result MUST be in range [0, 255] representing the count of leading zero bits before the most significant one bit.
If the stack is empty when CLZ is executed, standard EVM stack underflow behavior MUST apply and execution MUST revert.
Before the CLZ fork activation block, execution of opcode 0x1e MUST be treated as an invalid opcode causing execution to halt.
The gas cost of 5 for CLZ MUST be sufficient to prevent denial-of-service attacks on all supported hardware platforms.
All EVM implementations MUST execute CLZ in constant time regardless of input value to prevent timing side-channel attacks.
Opcode 0x1e MUST be currently unassigned and its allocation to CLZ MUST NOT conflict with any other proposed or existing EVM functionality.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-INPUT-LENGTH with len(data) != 213, the precompile MUST raise InvalidParameter and MUST NOT proceed to parameter parsing.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-FINAL-FLAG with f not in {0, 1}, the precompile MUST raise InvalidParameter.
After ACTION-EXECUTE-BLAKE2-COMPRESSION, the output MUST be the BLAKE2 compression result for the specified number of rounds with the given parameters.
After ACTION-CALCULATE-GAS-COST, the gas cost MUST equal rounds * GAS_BLAKE2_PER_ROUND exactly.
After ACTION-DEDUCT-GAS with insufficient gas, the precompile MUST enter out-of-gas state without producing any output.
When rounds parameter is 0, the BLAKE2F precompile MUST return the state h unchanged without raising an error.
Input to BLAKE2F MUST follow EIP-152 format: 4 bytes rounds + 64 bytes h + 128 bytes m + 8 bytes t_0 + 8 bytes t_1 + 1 byte f = 213 bytes total.
GAS_BLAKE2_PER_ROUND MUST equal 1 as specified in EIP-152.
The BLAKE2 compression function implementation MUST be cryptographically correct and match the BLAKE2b specification to prevent hash collisions.
An attacker MUST NOT be able to infer input data from BLAKE2F execution timing through side-channel observation.
The BLAKE2F precompile MUST execute in constant time regardless of input values to prevent timing attacks.
BLAKE2F input length MUST always be exactly 213 bytes; any other length MUST result in InvalidParameter exception.
The final block flag f at byte 212 MUST be exactly 0 or 1; any other value MUST result in InvalidParameter exception.
After ACTION-CONTRACT-EMIT-REQUEST, a request with valid request_type and request_data MUST be created and available for block inclusion.
After ACTION-APPEND-TO-BLOCK-REQUESTS, the request MUST be present in the block's accumulated request list and order MUST be preserved.
After ACTION-SORT-REQUESTS, all block requests MUST be ordered by request_type in ascending order.
After ACTION-FILTER-EMPTY-REQUESTS, only requests with non-empty request_data MUST remain for hash computation.
After ACTION-COMPUTE-FINAL-HASH, the requests_hash MUST be a valid 32-byte SHA256 digest of the concatenated individual request hashes.
After ACTION-EXPOSE-REQUESTS-TO-CL, all block requests MUST be accessible to the consensus layer via the Engine API.
After ACTION-CL-PROCESS-REQUESTS, the consensus state MUST be updated according to type-specific request handling rules.
After ACTION-COMPUTE-EMPTY-HASH for blocks with no requests, the requests_hash MUST equal SHA256 of the empty string.
Transactions from external submitters that trigger request generation MUST have their request data committed via SHA256 hash; the CL MUST validate requests independently of the EL.
Request data flowing from untrusted transaction submitters MUST be treated as opaque bytes; the EL MUST only provide integrity via hash commitment, not semantic validation.
Requests within the same request_type MUST be ordered by their generation order during transaction execution within the block.
Request validation MUST be delegated to the consensus layer; the execution layer MUST provide only integrity commitment via SHA256 hash.
Each request type MUST specify its own generation mechanism; EIP-7685 provides only the framework for request accumulation and hashing.
Consensus layer rejection of requests MUST NOT affect execution layer block validity; rejected requests are simply not applied to CL state.
The execution layer MUST correctly accumulate and hash all requests generated during block execution; omission or forgery MUST be detectable.
SHA256 MUST provide sufficient collision resistance for the requests_hash commitment to prevent forged request sets.
Future request types MUST be defined by subsequent EIPs that specify generation, validation, and processing rules.
The opaque byte format for request_data MUST be sufficient to support future encoding schemes without requiring framework changes.
Blob transactions from the mempool MUST have valid KZG commitments before being considered for block inclusion by the builder.
Blob transaction data from untrusted external sources MUST be validated for format and size before inclusion; builders MUST respect configured limits to ensure successful propagation.
After ACTION-CALCULATE-EFFECTIVE-LIMIT, the effective blob limit MUST equal min(MAX_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK, USER_CONFIGURED_MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK).
After ACTION-APPLY-MINIMUM-FLOOR, the effective blob limit MUST be at least 1 even if the computed minimum was 0.
After ACTION-BUILD-BLOCK-WITH-LIMIT, the block MUST contain no more blobs than the computed effective limit.
After ACTION-PROPAGATE-BLOCK with appropriately sized block, the network MUST accept the block without propagation timeout.
After ACTION-APPLY-DEFAULT with no user configuration, the blob limit MUST default to the current fork's maximum blob count.
USER_CONFIGURED_MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK MUST be specifiable via standard client configuration mechanisms (CLI flags, config file, or environment variable).
The comparison between user-configured and protocol blob limits MUST be done at the blob count level (MAX_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK / gas_per_blob).
Builders MUST accurately estimate their bandwidth capacity to configure the blob limit appropriately; misconfiguration risks propagation failures or revenue loss.
Network conditions MUST be sufficiently stable that a static blob limit configuration remains effective over the builder's operating period.
Local builders using blob limit configuration MUST NOT use it to artificially restrict blob inclusion for the purpose of manipulating blob gas prices.
Before processing a transaction from an external submitter, the signature s-value MUST be validated to not exceed secp256k1n/2 to prevent transaction malleability.

Contract creation transactions from external submitters MUST provide at least 53,000 gas and init code MUST be validated; insufficient gas for code storage MUST result in failure, not an empty contract.
Signed transaction data from untrusted external submitters MUST have all fields validated against protocol rules before any execution begins.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-S-VALUE with s > secp256k1n/2, the transaction MUST be rejected and MUST NOT produce any state modifications.
After ACTION-DEDUCT-INITIAL-GAS, exactly 53,000 gas MUST be deducted for transaction-based contract creation.
After ACTION-CHECK-FINAL-GAS with insufficient gas for code storage, contract creation MUST fail and the contract MUST NOT exist as an empty contract.
After ACTION-COMPUTE-NEW-DIFFICULTY, the block difficulty MUST be at least minDifficulty and MUST incorporate the timestamp-based adjustment factor and difficulty bomb.
The ecrecover precompile at address 0x01 MUST continue accepting both low and high s-values for legacy signature verification; this asymmetry with transaction validation is intentional.
When contract creation fails due to insufficient gas for code storage, standard out-of-gas semantics MUST apply: all provided gas is consumed with no refund.
The Homestead fork MUST activate atomically at HOMESTEAD_FORK_BLKNUM across all nodes to prevent chain splits and double-spend opportunities.
Block timestamps MUST NOT be manipulable by attackers to a degree that could significantly game the difficulty adjustment formula.
For all transactions after HOMESTEAD_FORK_BLKNUM, the signature s-value MUST satisfy 0 < s <= secp256k1n/2.
The difficulty adjustment factor MUST be bounded: max(1 - (block_timestamp - parent_timestamp) // 10, -99) to prevent extreme difficulty swings.
